parole.significato: to brag; to boast; to talk big

parole.significato: Synonym of pu'er (“a kind of tea”)

parole.significato: Chinese cabbage, Brassica rapa subsp. chinensis, an East Asian leafy vegetable related to the Western cabbage.

parole.significato: A particular defensive move in Wing Chun.

parole.significato: Comprising a mixture of various elements, mostly at random.

parole.significato: A Cantonese stuffed steamed baozi with char siu pork filling.

parole.significato: To inhale the vapor from heated morphine, heroin, oxycodone or opium that has been placed on a piece of foil.

parole.significato: A tight-fitting Chinese formal woman's dress, usually brightly coloured, patterned and/or embroidered, with a split at…

parole.significato: Expression of dismissal following an unmet expectation.

parole.significato: Relating to the Chaoshan region of China and/or its people.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 潮州 (ciu⁴ zau¹). Doublet of Chaozhou and Teochew.

parole.significato: A stir-fried vegetable dish, served with pieces of beef or pork in a semi-thick sauce, and often soy sauce.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 雜碎／杂碎 (zaap⁶ seoi³, “mixed and broken”).

parole.significato: A Chow Chow (Chinese breed of dog).
parole.testo: From Cantonese 周 (zau¹).

parole.significato: Overwhelming; demanding; intense.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese chur (coe²).

parole.significato: to shut up
parole.testo: Calque of Cantonese 收皮 (sau¹ pei⁴).

parole.significato: A dried seafood product made from scallops, used in Chinese cuisine.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 乾貝 /干贝 (gon1 bui3, literally “dried shell(fish)”).

parole.significato: A kind of open-air food stall.

parole.testo: From Cantonese 豆苗 (dau6 miu4).

parole.significato: A Cantonese-style meal traditionally eaten in the morning or early afternoon, comprising tea and food typically placed…

parole.significato: An indigenous inhabitant of the New Territories entitled to the building a village house under the Small House Policy.

parole.significato: Fuck you.

parole.significato: A kind of flat Cantonese egg noodles that is made by deep-frying.
parole.testo: Partial calque from Cantonese 伊府麵／伊府面 (ji1 fu2 min6).

parole.significato: Ew, yuck; expression of disgust.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 噫 (ji², interjection).

parole.significato: An egg-based dish containing vegetables and often bits of meat, originating in Guangdong and common in Chinese-American…
parole.testo: Partial calque of Cantonese 芙蓉蛋 (fu⁴ jung⁴ daan⁶⁻², “lotus egg”). From 蛋 (literally “egg”) + 芙蓉 (fu⁴ jung⁴, literally “lotus”)

parole.significato: A unit of length, equivalent to 0.1 tsun (0.01 chek), or 0.00371475 metres.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 分. Doublet of fen and hoon.

parole.significato: A Chinese gambling game in which coins or other small objects are placed upon a table, usually under a cup, and the pla…

parole.significato: a blue-green alga (Nostoc flagelliforme) used as a vegetable in Chinese cooking
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 髮菜 /发菜 (faat³ coi³).

parole.significato: Synonym of feng shui: the Cantonese-derived name.

parole.significato: A type of dumpling found in Cantonese cuisine, popular in Chinese New Year celebrations.

parole.significato: Synonym of congee.

parole.significato: A catty, legally defined as 0.60478982 kilograms.

parole.significato: Nervous, anxious, keyed up

parole.significato: A Chinese fortune telling practice involving numbered sticks that represent particular answers to questions.

parole.significato: to finish, to complete

parole.significato: A set of four identical tiles.

parole.significato: A variety of smoked black tea (Camellia sinensis), originally from the Wuyi region of the Fujian province of southern C…

parole.significato: Synonym of daikon, particularly its Cantonese varieties.

parole.significato: An errand boy, especially in Chinatown.

parole.significato: A food consisting of meat, vegetables, etc. served on a skewer for dipping into sauce.

parole.significato: Any member of the species Eriobotrya japonica of trees (Japanese medlar, Chinese plum, Japanese plum).

parole.significato: constable of Chinese descent

parole.significato: Asserts that there is a straightforward or self-evident reason for something.

parole.significato: A type of wooden dummy designed to be kicked and punched in Wing Chun kung fu training.

parole.significato: To be unable to bear (the sight of) something anymore; to refuse to be involved further; to be disinclined to continue…

parole.significato: A Chinese lottery game popular in Oceania in the 19th century, involving tickets marked with rows of Chinese characters.

parole.significato: An alloy of zinc, copper and nickel, closely resembling silver, of Chinese origin; any of a number of similar alloys de…
parole.testo: Anglicisation of Cantonese 白銅／白铜 (baak6 tung4, “white copper”).

parole.significato: To go out on a date with someone whom one is romantically involved with.

parole.significato: A gambling game, originally Chinese, in which bets are laid on secretly selected numbers.

parole.significato: Having no money; broke; bankrupt.
parole.testo: Cantonese 仆街 (puk1 gaai1, “fall onto street, drop dead, go to hell, [Singapore, Malaysia] to have no money)”), from 仆 (puk1, “fall”) + 街 (gaai1, “street”).

parole.significato: The calabash or bottle gourd.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 蒲瓜 (pou4 gwaa1).

parole.significato: A set of three identical tiles.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 碰 (pung³).

parole.significato: A group of people who moved to Hong Kong during the Song Dynasty.
parole.testo: From a historical pronunciation of Cantonese 本地 (bun² dei⁶, “local”).

parole.significato: A Hawaiian noodle soup garnished with green onions.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 細 /细 (sai³, “thin”) + 麵 /面 (min⁶, “noodle”).

parole.significato: A type of suit worn in China, consisting of a shirt with a high neckline bound down the middle with tassels, and trouse…
parole.testo: From Cantonese 衫褲／衫裤 (saam¹ fu³, “shirt (and) pants”).

parole.significato: A triple-distilled variety of rice-based baijiu.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 三燒 /三烧 (“thrice-burnt”), a former name of 三蒸酒 (sānzhēngjiǔ, “thrice-distilled alcohol”).

parole.significato: A dish of boiled or steamed chicken wrapped in lettuce, served with garlic sauce or ginger sauce.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 三水 (saam¹ seoi²) + chicken.

parole.significato: A Chinese female immigrant who came to Malaya or Singapore between the 1920s and 1940s in search of construction or ind…
parole.testo: From Cantonese 三水 (saam¹ seoi²).

parole.significato: Blood cockles; ark clams (as food)
parole.testo: From Cantonese 螄蚶 /蛳蚶 (si¹⁻³ ham¹).

parole.significato: crack seed
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 西梅 (sai1 mui4-2, “prune”), via Hawaii.

parole.significato: A dog of a distinctive breed with deep wrinkles, especially when young, a blue-black tongue, and a rough short coat.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 沙皮 (saa¹ pei⁴, “sandpapery skin”).

parole.significato: To urinate; to pee.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 𭉝𭉝 (syu⁴ syu⁴⁻²). Compare Portuguese xixi, and Hawaiian English shishi.

parole.significato: A Thai-themed nightclub or disco at which people dance to music and pay a hostess to talk to or drink with them by buyi…
parole.testo: From Siam (“historical name of Thailand”) and Cantonese 吊 (diu3, “to hang”), referring to the flower garlands.

parole.significato: A Chinese game of chance involving betting on the outcome of rolling three dice.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 骰寶／骰宝 (sik1 bou2).

parole.significato: A master or teacher in the context of martial arts, especially kung fu and tai chi.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 師傅／师傅 (si1 fu6-2, “master”) and 師父／师父 (si1 fu6-2, “my master”), both also conveying the sense of teacher.

parole.significato: A gourd of species Luffa acutangula, whose fruits are eaten when half-ripe and when mature can be dried out to form a l…
parole.testo: Sinkwa likely from Cantonese 勝瓜 /胜瓜 (sing³ gwaa¹).

parole.significato: A kind of barbecue sauce used in Cantonese cuisine.
parole.testo: Cantonese 燒烤 /烧烤 (siu¹ haau¹)

parole.significato: Meat roasted on spits over an open fire or wood burning rotisserie oven, as in Cantonese cuisine.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 燒味 /烧味 (siu¹ mei⁶⁻²). Doublet of shaowei.

parole.significato: Roast pork in Chinese cuisine.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 燒肉／烧肉 (siu1 juk6, “roasted pig”).

parole.significato: Dumbass; idiot
parole.testo: From Cantonese 傻閪 /傻𲈹 (so⁴ hai¹, “stupid cunt”).

parole.significato: Synonym of marbled goby (“Oxyeleotris marmorata”).
parole.testo: From Cantonese 筍殼 /笋壳 (seon² hok³) and Hakka 筍殼 /笋壳 (sun³ hog⁵).

parole.significato: In American Chinese cuisine, minced meat or vegetables.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 鬆 /松 (sung¹).

parole.significato: Insane, crazy, screwed up.
parole.testo: From Cantonese short (sot¹, “crazy”), itself a clipping of English short circuit.

parole.significato: Any of several varieties of aromatic black tea from China.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 小種 /小种 (siu² zung², “subvariety”). See also Hokkien 小種茶 /小种茶 (sió-chióng-tê).

parole.significato: Scrotum; testicles.
parole.testo: Calque of Cantonese 春袋 (ceon¹ doi⁶, ceon¹ doi⁶⁻²). Popularized by The Conmen in Vegas (1999).

parole.significato: A Cantonese dish consisting of mixed meat and vegetables, often in combination with noodles, rice, or soup.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 什錦／什锦 (sap6 gam2).

parole.significato: Any of various gold or silver ingots used as currency in imperial China.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 細絲 /细丝 (sai³ si¹, “fine silk”), variously explained as owing to the bullion's ability to be worked into fine strands or from the resemblance of its luster.

parole.significato: A foreign businessman in China; a tycoon.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 大班 (daai⁶ baan¹, “big shot, rich businessman”), originally as taepan. Related to tycoon, from Japanese 大君(たいくん) (taikun).

parole.significato: large Chinese steamed stuffed bun
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 大包 (daai⁶ baau¹).

parole.significato: Synonym of picul, a unit of weight, particularly in Cantonese contexts.
parole.testo: From the Cantonese pronunciation of 擔 /担.

parole.significato: Synonym of picul, particularly in Cantonese contexts.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 擔／担 (daam3).

parole.significato: A member of a group of people in southern China who traditionally live on junks.
parole.testo: Likely from Cantonese 蜑家 (daan6 gaa1).

parole.significato: A fermented black soybean sauce.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 豆豉 (dau⁶ si⁶).

parole.significato: To order (food) as takeaway; to pack food so it can be consumed elsewhere.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 打包 (daa³ baau¹, “to pack”).

parole.significato: Brassica rapa subsp. narinosa (syns. Brassica narinosa, Brasica rapa var. narinosa, Brassica rapa var. rosularis), an A…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 塌菜 (taap3 coi3, “collapsed vegetable”).

parole.significato: Synonym of Taishanese.
parole.testo: From Toisan + -ese. From Cantonese 臺山 /台山 (toi⁴ saan¹).

parole.significato: A Chinese lineage organization responsible for managing ancestral land.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 堂 (tong⁴).

parole.significato: A tuition fee collected by public sector schools.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 堂費 /堂费 (tong4 fai3).

parole.significato: A tenement building, found in Southern China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 唐樓 /唐楼 (tong4 lau4-2).

parole.significato: A high-quality white raw silk from Zhejiang, China, produced mostly for export.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 七里 (cat¹ lei⁵, literally “seven li”), a placename.

parole.significato: A meal consisting of rice and two side dishes, often sold at a low price; economy rice.
parole.testo: Calque of Cantonese 兩餸飯 /两𩠌饭 (loeng⁵ sung³ faan⁶, literally “two-dish rice”).

parole.significato: What the hell are you saying?
parole.testo: Partial calque of Cantonese 噏乜春 (ngap¹ mat¹ ceon¹, “what the hell are you babbling about”, literally “what testicles are you babbling about”), where 春 (ceon¹) is a homograph meaning both “testicles” and “spring (season)”. By surface analysis, Cantonese up + what + spring.

parole.significato: Wow!; whoa! (expressing surprise, gratification, exhaustion or exasperation)
parole.testo: From Cantonese 嘩 /哗 (waa³) or Mandarin 哇 (wa).

parole.significato: A tree, Clausena lansium, native to Southern China and Indochina.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 黃皮 /黄皮 (wong⁴ pei⁴⁻², “wampee”, literally “yellow skin”).

parole.significato: wonton (Chinese dumpling)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 雲吞 /云吞 (wan⁴ tan¹).

parole.significato: Almond-battered deep-fried chicken breast (white meat).
parole.testo: From Cantonese 鍋燒雞 /锅烧鸡.

parole.significato: A popular style of kung fu.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 詠春 /咏春 (wing6 ceon1), from 詠 /咏 (wing6, “praise”) + 春 (ceon1, “spring”).

parole.significato: A large, round-bottomed cooking pan used in East Asian cooking.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 鑊 /镬 (wok⁶).

parole.significato: The slightly seared flavour imparted to food that has been traditionally cooked in a seasoned wok.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 鑊氣 /镬气 (wok6 hei3).

parole.significato: Napa cabbage.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 黃芽白 /黄芽白 (wong⁴ ngaa⁴ baak⁶).

parole.significato: A Chinese dumpling, often stuffed with varieties of meat or seafood and vegetables.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Cantonese 雲吞 /云吞 (wan⁴ tan¹, wan⁴ tan⁴).

parole.significato: Synonym of special fried rice.
parole.testo: Partial calque of Mandarin 揚州炒飯 /扬州炒饭 (Yángzhōu chǎofàn), from Cantonese 揚州炒飯 /扬州炒饭 (joeng⁴ zau¹ caau² faan⁶).

parole.significato: internal heat
parole.testo: From Cantonese 熱氣 /热气 (jit6 hei3).

parole.significato: A strong desire, urge, or yearning.
parole.testo: Origin uncertain, but probably from Cantonese 癮 /瘾 (jan⁵, “craving”) originally in reference to opium addiction, 煙癮 /烟瘾 (jin¹ jan⁵) or 菸癮 /烟瘾 (jin¹ jan⁵): 煙 /烟 (jin¹), 菸 /烟 (jin¹, “smoke, specifically opium”). Compare the later yen (“opium”) and yen-yen.

parole.significato: An administrative division.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 約 /约 (joek3).

parole.significato: One's fate and how one is treated in life depends on one's looks.
parole.termine_origine: 你的樣子如何，你的命運也必如何

catena.termine: 你的樣子如何，你的命運也必如何

parole.testo: Calque of Cantonese 你的樣子如何，你的命運也必如何 /你的样子如何，你的命运也必如何 (nei⁵ dik¹ joeng⁶ zi² jyu⁴ ho⁴, nei⁵ dik¹ ming⁶ wan⁶ jaa⁵ bit¹ jyu⁴ ho⁴, “And as thy face, so shall thy fate be”), modified from a verse in the Bible 你的日子如何，你的力量也必如何 (“And as thy days, so shall thy strength be”).

parole.significato: A variety of Brassica known as Brassica rapa subsp. oleifera syn. Brassa campestris, related to choy sum and bok choy.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 油菜 (jau4 coi3).

parole.significato: A beverage made by mixing coffee with Hong Kong-style milk tea.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 鴛鴦 /鸳鸯 (jyun¹ joeng¹).

parole.significato: A traditional (usually daytime, sometimes nighttime) Chinese meal, consisting of several small courses (dim sum) and Ch…
parole.testo: From Cantonese 飲茶／饮茶 (jam2 caa4).

parole.significato: To invite; to meet up.
parole.testo: From Cantonese 約 /约 (joek³).

parole.significato: A Cantonese dish, composed of stir-fried wide noodles, bean sprouts, and meat or tofu.
parole.testo: From either Taishanese 炒粉 (cau² fun²) or Cantonese 炒粉 (caau² fan²).

parole.significato: To kneel and bow low enough to touch one’s forehead to the ground.
parole.testo: From either Cantonese 叩頭 /叩头 (kau³ tau⁴) or Mandarin 叩頭 /叩头 (kòutóu). Literally, “knock head”.

parole.significato: I (or we) have not seen you for a long time.
parole.testo: Uncertain. Possibly a calque of Cantonese 好耐冇見 /好耐冇见 (hou² noi⁶ mou⁵ gin³), Mandarin 很久沒見 /很久没见 (hěnjiǔméijiàn), Mandarin 好久不見 /好久不见 (hǎojiǔbùjiàn), or similar expressions in other Chinese varieties, comparable to no can do or chop-chop – if so, most likely US Chinatown origin, or, alternatively, Br

parole.significato: A superior kind of souchong tea.
parole.testo: Possibly from either Hokkien 包種茶 /包种茶 (pau-chióng-tê, literally “tea of the wrapped kind”) or Cantonese 包種 /包种 (baau¹ zung², literally “the wrapped kind”).
